messages:
maya: Quick perf note: FlashFlux v2 shows SMEM blowup on A100 when seq_len >= 2048. KV warmup also spikes memory traffic. Anyone else seeing this?
sam: saw weird bank-conflict + L2 saturation last night, thought it was our scheduler change. can you paste perf counters?
maya: pasted a quick run below from nsight (short): 
```text
SMEM_Usage: 256KB -> 512KB per block
shared_bank_conflicts: 42%
l2_read_throughput: 120 GB/s -> 220 GB/s
```
chris: @maya can you rerun with batch_size=1 and cache_disabled=true? want to isolate KV warmup.
maya: running now. command:
```bash
./bench_attn --kernel=flashflux_v2 --seq=2048 --batch=1 --kwarm=false --nvprof
```
ci-bot: bench started on runner-12 (a100-40g). job: #3821
eva: looked at trace — pattern looks like repeated 32B strides touching same bank after tiling change. suspect tiler now emits stride=32 for paged shards.
sam: could be our "fused pipeline" reorder. If tiler reduces tilesize to 32 it will thrash smem banks. check kernel params: tile_x=32 tile_y=8?
maya: here's a heap of nvprof counters from the run (trimmed):
```text
sm_efficiency: 67%
gld_request: 1.2M
gst_request: 800K
shared_load_replay: 230K
achieved_occupancy: 0.72
```
chris: occupancy 0.72 ok but replay high. maybe register pressure causing spills -> shared load replay.
sam: try increasing blockSize to 256 and bumping prefetch pipeline stages by +1. also try fallback kernel flashflux_v1 to compare.
maya: ran v1 fallback, results: latency +6% but mem traffic down ~35%. seems like v2 aggressive fusion is hurting for long seqs.
eva: for short seq (<512) v2 still wins. so need dynamic kernel selection by seq_len+kv_state.
maya: proposal: add heuristic: if seq_len >= 1024 and kv_warmup_steps > 32 then prefer flashflux_v1; also add smem_bank_stride sanity check in tiler to avoid 32-byte stride on a100.
chris: +1. Also log a perf tag in traces so we can roll forward if we test tiler patch.
maya: I'll open a tiny PR with a nudge to tiler and heuristic. dropping perf dumps in the PR.
sam: thx. can we also add a microbatching fallback so the frontend can choose smaller sub-batches to avoid SMEM thrash?
maya: yes, we can. filing a follow-up issue for batching heuristics.
ci-bot: created issue #778: "adaptive microbatch fallback for FlashFlux SMEM thrash" and PR #492 opened by maya
chris: cool. @maya can you add a short reproducer script to the PR so QA can run on different GPU types? :eyes: 
maya: will do. thanks.
